content:
After the man who deliberately broke the Sabbath was judged, Yahweh gave Israel a very simple but powerful command. He told them to make tassels on the corners of their garments and to place a blue cord in the tassel.

Then Yahweh Himself explained why, saying, "You shall have the tassel, that you may look upon it and remember all the commandments of Yahweh and do them" (Numbers 15:39). Notice the order: look, remember, and do. The tassel was something their eyes could see. What their eyes saw was meant to awaken their memory, and what they remembered was meant to change how they lived. Yahweh knew how easily the human heart forgets. Israel could see the Red Sea open one day and grumble for water the next. They could eat manna from heaven and still question God's goodness. So, Yahweh placed a reminder upon the very garment they wore, and it travelled everywhere they went. Before their feet carried them somewhere they should not go, before their hands did something forbidden, and before their eyes followed something the heart desired, there hung a reminder: remember Yahweh, remember His commandments, remember that you belong to Him. For God continued, "That you may not follow the harlotry to which your own heart and your own eyes are inclined" (Numbers 15:39). The problem was not merely forgetfulness of the mind; the heart and the eyes could lead them astray. The tassel interrupted that process, bringing God's Word back into the mind before desire could become disobedience.

Now this gives us a beautiful picture for us, the New Creation. We do not wear a literal thread of blue upon the corner of our clothing, yet Yahweh has given us many reminders to keep His Word before our eyes and to turn our hearts back to Him whenever they begin to wander. Israel could wear a tassel while carrying a rebellious heart, and in the same way, merely owning a Bible, wearing a cross, attending meetings, being baptized, or taking the bread and cup cannot replace obedience. The reminder has done its work only when looking produces remembering, and remembering produces obedience.

So what are the things the New Creation can continually look toward and remember? Let us consider five of them.

**1. Look to Christ - Remember Whom We Follow**

The greatest object before our eyes is not a thread, but a Person. The Scripture tells us we are "looking unto Jesus, the author and finisher of our faith" (Hebrews 12:2). When the world attracts our eyes, we look again to Christ. When suffering makes us weary, we look to Christ. When temptation promises us pleasure, we look to Christ. When pride tells us to live for ourselves, we look to Christ. The tassel directed Israel's mind away from its wandering heart and back toward Yahweh; in the same way, our very first and greatest tassel is the continual remembrance of Christ Himself. Whenever our eyes are drawn toward the world, we deliberately turn them once more toward Him.

**2. Look to the Cross - Remember Whom We Belong To**

The cross tells us that our life is no longer our own. The Scripture says, "You were bought at a price; therefore, glorify God in your body" (1 Corinthians 6:20). Israel's tassel reminded them, "You belong to Yahweh." For us, the cross continually reminds us that we were purchased, and that we now belong entirely to God through Christ. When our hands want to perform a sin,
we remember the cross. When our feet want to carry us into the world,we remember the cross. When our tongue wants to wound another person,we remember the cross. The cross says to us, again and again: you were bought, and you belong to Christ.

**3. Remember the Blood - Remember the Cost**

We were not cleansed cheaply. The Scripture says, "The blood of Jesus Christ His Son cleanses us from all sin" (1 John 1:7). So, before we ever deliberately return to a sin, we remember what that sin cost. Christ gave His very life to wash us. The blood should never become something common or cheap in our minds. Because we were redeemed at such a great price, we must never treat sin casually, nor treat the blood of Christ as an ordinary thing. When temptation whispers that one sin will not matter, the memory of the blood restrains us,
for we remember the terrible price at which our cleansing was bought.

**4. Remember Your Baptism - Remember the Life You Left**

Our baptism is another powerful reminder. The Scripture says, "We were buried with Him through baptism into death... even so we also should walk in newness of life" (Romans 6:4). When Egypt begins to look attractive again,
we remember our baptism. I left Egypt. The old life was buried. I rose to walk in newness of life. The New Creation should never go back and dig up what has already been buried. When the old ways call to us and the world seems pleasant again, the memory of our baptism answers that we have already died to that life and risen to walk in a new one.

**5. Look at the Bread and Cup - Remember Him**

Here Christ Himself actually commands us to remember, for He said, "Do this in remembrance of Me" (Luke 22:19). We see the bread. We see the cup. And we remember. His body was given for us. His blood established the covenant.

We belong to God through Christ. Israel looked upon the tassel and remembered Yahweh's covenant commandments; the New Creation looks upon the bread and the cup and remembers the One who gave Himself for us. For just as Israel had something they could see that brought the covenant back to mind, so Christ gave us a visible act, the broken bread and the poured cup, that turns our remembrance directly to His sacrificed body and His covenant blood.

So, these five reminders continually surround our New Creation walk. Christ reminds us of whom we follow. The cross reminds us of whom we belong to. The blood reminds us of what our cleansing cost. Baptism reminds us of the life we left behind. And the bread and cup remind us of Christ's sacrifice and His covenant. But these tassels do not hang by themselves. They hang upon the garment of a changed life, the new man we have put on, for the Scripture says, "You have put off the old man with his deeds and have put on the new man" (Colossians 3:9-10), and again, "For as many of you as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ" (Galatians 3:27). The tassel meant nothing when it hung upon a heart that had not changed; so, our reminders mean nothing unless the garment beneath them is the new life in Christ. And here we come to the blue. Under the Law, Israel wore only a single thread of blue, the colour of the sanctuary and the priesthood, the colour that lifted the eye up to the throne of God. But the New Creation is not given merely a thread of blue upon the corner. We ourselves are called to be the priesthood, for Peter says, "You are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people"

(1 Peter 2:9). What was only a small blue cord for Israel has become our very calling. We are clothed in the new man and marked out for a heavenly, priestly holiness, our eyes lifted up to where Christ our great High Priest has entered before us. So let the whole garment of our life be woven for heaven above and reach out to every corner below, that we may remember, obey, and be holy unto our God. Tomorrow, Yahweh willing, we will study how to train the mind to remember before we act.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our God, who clothes His people in the new life of Christ,
Give us eyes that look continually to Christ, the author and finisher of our faith.

Let the cross remind us of whom we belong to, and the blood remind us what our cleansing cost.

Let our baptism remind us of the Egypt we have left and never dig up what You have buried.

And at the bread and the cup, let us truly remember the One who gave Himself for us.

Clothe us in the new man, and mark us as Your royal priesthood, holy unto You.

"Set your minds on things above, not on the things of the earth." Colossians 3:2

In Chrit’s name, our great High Priest, we pray. Amen.
